title: Sunil Narine Becomes First Overseas Player to Play 200 IPL Matches as KKR Mark Eden Gardens Century
excerpt: The 37-year-old Trinidadian all-rounder reached a historic milestone as Kolkata Knight Riders played their 100th IPL match at Eden Gardens in a do-or-die clash against Gujarat Titans.
body:
Kolkata Knight Riders and their talismanic all-rounder Sunil Narine etched their names into IPL history on Saturday, as the franchise played its **100th match at Eden Gardens** — becoming only the second team after Royal Challengers Bengaluru (at M. Chinnaswamy Stadium) to reach the landmark at a single venue — while Narine became the **first overseas player to appear in 200 IPL matches**.

The milestones arrived at a charged moment in the IPL 2026 season. KKR entered **Match 60** against Gujarat Titans needing to win all their remaining games to keep playoff hopes alive, while GT — on a five-match winning streak — were looking to become the first team to secure a 2026 playoff berth.

### A Career Like No Other

Narine's journey from a mystery spinner plucked from Trinidad & Tobago cricket to one of the IPL's most decorated overseas players is without parallel. First signed by KKR ahead of the 2012 season, the Trinidadian has spent his entire IPL career with the franchise — a loyalty virtually unheard of in modern franchise cricket.

Over those **200 matches**, Narine has accumulated over **200 IPL wickets** with a miserly economy rate of **6.51** — among the lowest for any spinner with a comparable volume of matches. But the numbers alone undersell the transformation. Once a pure bowler who batted at No. 11, Narine reinvented himself as a destructive opening batsman, memorably scoring a century (109 off 56 balls) and taking five wickets in the same match — a feat no other player has achieved in IPL history.

At 37, Narine's body is showing the strain of being both a frontline spinner and a power-hitting opener in the world's most demanding T20 league. Speculation about retirement has swirled all season, and the Eden Gardens faithful gave him a standing ovation before the toss.

### KKR's 100th at the Fortress

Eden Gardens, with its **66,000-seat capacity** and iconic atmosphere, has been KKR's home since the IPL's inception in 2008. Reaching 100 matches at the venue underscores the franchise's deep roots in Kolkata's sporting culture — a relationship cemented by the Shah Rukh Khan ownership era and sustained through multiple coaching changes, title wins in **2012, 2014 and 2024**, and the enduring presence of players like Narine and Andre Russell.

Before the match, former KKR captain **Eoin Morgan** rang the Eden Gardens bell in a ceremony marking the centenary. Captain **Ajinkya Rahane** confirmed the return of spinner **Varun Chakravarthy** from a leg injury, reuniting KKR's primary spin partnership with Narine for the business end of the season.

### The Playoff Picture

GT skipper **Shubman Gill** won the toss and chose to bowl, citing overnight rain and a sticky pitch. Gujarat Titans sit atop the table and need just one more win to confirm their playoff place. KKR, by contrast, face elimination if they lose — their season on a knife's edge despite a recent four-match winning streak that briefly revived their campaign.

### Why It Matters to the Diaspora

IPL milestones resonate far beyond India's borders. For the millions of Indian Americans who follow the tournament through **JioCinema** and Star Sports streams — often scheduling their mornings around IST evening matches — Narine's landmark is a reminder of how deeply the IPL has woven itself into global cricket culture. The Trinidadian, who has made Kolkata his adopted home, embodies the tournament's promise: that talent, regardless of nationality, can build a legacy in Indian cricket.

### What's Next

KKR need to win their remaining three matches to have any shot at the playoffs. GT, if they secure a top-two finish, earn the safety net of an extra match in the knockouts. With the league phase entering its final week, every result now cascades through the points table — and at Eden Gardens on Saturday, history was being made regardless of the scoreboard.
